### 1. Calculation and Parameters
* Diameter of circle ($d$) = $50\text{ mm}$, Radius ($r$) = $25\text{ mm}$
* Circumference ($\pi d$) = $\pi \times 50 ≈ 157.08\text{ mm}$ (This is the length of the path of one complete revolution along the horizontal baseline).

### 2. Steps to Draw the Cycloid
1. Draw a horizontal baseline equal to the circumference ($157.08\text{ mm}$). Let's call it $AB$.
2. Draw a vertical line $AC$ equal to the diameter ($50\text{ mm}$) perpendicular to $AB$.
3. Complete the rectangle and draw the center line at height $R = 25\text{ mm}$ parallel to $AB$. Center of the generating circle moves along this line.
4. Draw a semicircle on $AC$ (representing the generating circle's path) and divide it into $12$ equal parts (or $8$ parts).
5. Project these division points horizontally across the rectangular length. Divide line $AB$ into the exact same number of equal parts ($12$ divisions).
6. With centers $C_1, C_2, \dots$ on the center line and radius equal to $R$, draw arcs passing through the projected height points to locate points $P_1, P_2, \dots$ on the cycloid curve.
7. Smoothly join points $P_0, P_1, P_2, \dots$ with a French curve to get the cycloid.

### 3. Tangent and Normal at $35\text{ mm}$ above the Baseline
1. Draw a horizontal line parallel to the baseline at a height of $35\text{ mm}$ to intersect the cycloid curve at point $P$.
2. With center $P$ and radius equal to radius of the generating circle ($25\text{ mm}$), cut an arc on the center line of the generating circle to locate the center $C'$ of the rolling circle.
3. Drop a vertical line from $C'$ to meet the baseline at point $Q$.
4. Join $Q$ with $P$ and extend it to get the **Normal** line.
5. Draw a line perpendicular to the normal passing through point $P$ to obtain the **Tangent**.
proTip: Ensure the generating circle is divided into 12 equal angular intervals for smooth and symmetrical plotting of the cycloid curve.
